post.description:
Saves a full-text search to watch for new filings. With a `webhook`, FinancialFilings runs it about once an hour, sending the filings added since the last run to your webhook as one `saved_search.hits` event (at most `max_hits_per_run` hits, oldest first; `more` counts the rest, which the next runs send). Without one, pull the new hits yourself with `POST /filings/search/saved/{id}/new/`. Either way the search starts from when it is created: run `GET /filings/search/` for what already matches. Each run or pull that returns hits is billed as one page of `GET /filings/search/`; one with no new hits, or whose delivery fails, is free.

Free: never charged credits.

post.description: Returns the filings added to FinancialFilings that match this saved search and that no earlier pull returned, oldest first, at most `max_hits_per_run`, and records them as returned: each filing is returned once. That includes a filing released long ago that reached FinancialFilings since the last pull, and one whose text arrived late (within 48 hours). Use this instead of re-running `GET /filings/search/` with a moving `release_datetime_from`, which misses both. When `more` is above 0, pull again for the rest. Only for an active saved search with no webhook (409 `delivers_to_webhook` or `saved_search_paused` otherwise). The response is the delivery: hits it returned are not returned again by a later pull, so keep them. If a response was lost, `repeat_last_pull=true` returns the hits of the last pull that returned any, again: no search, no snippets, nothing recorded, free. Billed as one page of `GET /filings/search/` when it returns at least one hit; an empty pull is free.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique integer value identifying this saved search.

parameters.name: repeat_last_pull
parameters.description: true: return the hits of the last pull that returned any, again (with `pulled_at`), instead of pulling. Not billed.

* `` - Never run
* `delivered` - Delivered
* `no_new_hits` - No new hits
* `delivery_failed` - Delivery failed
* `search_unavailable` - Search unavailable

count.description: Total matching results. Exact for cheap queries, an estimate on broad or expensive ones. Do not use it to decide when to stop: follow `next` until it is null.

params.description: The search, as the query parameters of `GET /filings/search/`: `q` (a string or a list of up to 5 alternatives) and any filter that endpoint takes, e.g. `{"q": ["going concern", "material uncertainty"], "countries": "DE,FR"}`. Checked exactly as that endpoint checks them. `added_to_platform_from`/`_to`, `ordering`, `page`, `page_size` and `view` are set by each run and cannot be saved.

webhook.description: The id of your webhook that receives each run's `saved_search.hits` event. Leave it out (or null) to pull the new hits yourself with `POST /filings/search/saved/{id}/new/` instead; such a search is never run on a schedule.

is_active.description: `false` pauses the search. At most 20 active per account.

max_hits_per_run.description: Hits per delivery or pull, 1-200 (default 50). Further new hits are counted in `more` and delivered by the next runs (or pulls), oldest first.

cursor.description: Filings added to FinancialFilings at or after this time (minus a short lookback for filings whose text arrived late) are searched by the next run or pull. It moves only after a delivery succeeds, or a pull returns hits.

match.description: Snippets, as `match` on `GET /filings/search/`; null when they were not computed.

more.description: New hits past `max_hits_per_run`, left for the next runs. A lower bound when `capped`.

capped.description: True: more than the first 1000 matches by relevance fell in the window, so some may never be delivered. Narrow the search.

more.description: New hits past `max_hits_per_run`, left for the next pulls: pull again now to get them. A lower bound when `capped`.

capped.description: True: more than the first 1000 matches by relevance fell in the window, so some may never be returned. Narrow the search.

scan_complete.description: False: the search stopped before checking every candidate, so more new filings may exist than were returned. With no hits, nothing was recorded; pull again later.

pulled_at.description: Only with `repeat_last_pull=true`: when that pull ran (null: no pull has returned hits yet). That response carries `saved_search`, `hits` and `pulled_at` only.
